items.title: Pigeons Playing Ping Pong- Jeremy Schon & Greg Ormont interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 8, 2024
items.q: The Who’s guitarist, Pete Townshend, was in the pit playing with the band and I was about ten years old.

ctx.x: Did either of you have an experience, if you look back when you were kids, when we were kids we didn’t know what the word “epiphany” meant. But now we do and is there anything that happened that really caught your attention and set you on this musical path?

You know that comes up a lot and you’re right, you don’t realize it when it happens but if you start to look back there’s some moments that kind of seems like it sets you on this path. For me, I mean when I was five years old, in kindergarten, everyone in my school would be in the kindergarten circus, and that would mean there would be dogs on — or clowns on tricycles or whatever. And I was cast as the doggie in the window. And my big line would be, you know, [sings] “How much is that doggie in the window” I’d go…

arf.” Right? Very cute. And people — I remember being on stage and seeing a positive reaction there and that was what got me into — I did a lot of musical theater from age 5 to 17. And that next year my best friend who’s still one of my best friends for life, his mother did all of the directing for the musical theater in our community so between catching the bug and then meeting him and starting to do all the plays I found myself singing for the rest of my life. The second piece that I look back on is I grew up…
